name: Magnetic Bridge
description: Foundational bridge module mapping magnetic polarity (N/S) to binary states (0/1) through field resonance and interference patterns. Constructive interference encodes 1, destructive encodes 0. Field density gradients map geometric intensity and spacing to information density. The read/write protocol for silicon lattice computation.

core_attributes.pattern: polarity-to-binary translation, field interference encoding, density gradient mapping

scope.definition: Bit error rate of magnetic polarity-encoded information storage — probability that a stored magnetic bit is correctly read after 10 years in stable environmental conditions.

evidence.source: Charap & Lu (1997) 'Thermal stability of recorded information at high densities', IEEE Transactions on Magnetics 33:978-983; NIST magnetic recording reliability studies.
cross_domain_examples: high-coercivity hard disk magnetic domains: BER < 10⁻¹⁵ over 10-year storage under controlled conditions
Earth magnetic field reversal preserves paleomagnetic record in basalt for 10⁹ years — natural encoding fidelity
optical data storage: comparable long-term stability but with thermal degradation at different rate

scope.falsifiability: If BER in standard magnetic storage media exceeds 10⁻¹⁰ per bit per decade at standard conditions, the 10-year stability claim fails.
scope.measurement_limits: Stability depends on coercivity and grain volume — superparamagnetic limit at ~5 nm grain size. High-density recording approaches this limit, creating tension between density and longevity.
